# Orita Roadmap — Fencepost (demo #1 of the platform)

> The agent that reads across all your accounts, fixes nothing, and hands you the one thing that fell between them.

**The town's work queue. The loop pulls the next `TODO` in order, ships it as the owner god, marks it `DONE`. No idle cycles. Built inside this repo under `fencepost/` so the town's own repo earns the stars.**

**Row numbers are unique, 1..N, no gaps, no repeats** (`test_wip_reclaim_check.py`'s `test_real_roadmap_has_no_row_number_gaps_up_to_its_own_highest_task` enforces this in `dawn-run`). A same-hour addendum (e.g. a background test suite that finishes after the row's own `DONE`) is appended INTO that task's existing row, never written as a second row reusing the same number — task 1117 fixed the one hour this slipped (task 1116's own addendum landed as a duplicate `| 1116 |` row and broke `dawn-run`'s `the-oath` job; merged back into a single row, sealed history left visible in both commits).

## Non-negotiable design constraints (from the Hand)
1. **Read-only.** Only read/list Arcade scopes. Fencepost fixes nothing; the final action is always the human's.
2. **No grading/competing.** Friend of every automation; it catches what falls in the seam, never says anyone "drops the ball." Name and rank no one.
3. **False positives are fatal.** Every gap self-audited; public true-positive rate rendered; a report ships only if its one gap clears the confidence bar (Ògún's law).
4. **Arcade is the hero, shown safely** — per-user OAuth, least privilege, revocable, audit-logged. This protects Arcade's look; treat it as the point.
5. **Written back to a place the user owns.** The Gap Ledger is a durable record, not a diff.

Real find this hour, not the usual no-op: `tools/sync_checkout.sh ~/orita main` refused live with "diverged ... neither is an ancestor of the other -- resolve by hand" even though `origin/main` had only moved forward by an ordinary fast-forward. Root cause: the checkout was a shallow clone (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` true, `.git/shallow` holding two old boundary commits); `git merge-base --is-ancestor` cannot see past a shallow horizon, so a perfectly ordinary fast-forward whose true common ancestor sits before that horizon reads as "neither is ancestor" -- the script's own genuine-divergence case, fired on nothing that had actually diverged. Confirmed with `git fetch --unshallow`: `merge-base` succeeded immediately afterward with no other change. Fixed `tools/sync_checkout.sh` to detect a shallow checkout and unshallow it before either ancestor check runs (both the attached-branch and detached-HEAD code paths share the one fetch call now). Reproduced the exact disconnected-shallow-islands shape by hand in a disposable repo (two separate `--depth 1` fetches, one at an old commit, one at the new tip, no shared history fetched in between) and proved the old script refused it while the fixed script recovers it correctly (`fast-forwarded`, no `diverged`). Added `TestShallowCloneFalseDivergence` to `tests/test_sync_checkout.py` encoding that same reproduction so it never has to be re-diagnosed from scratch; all 12 sync-checkout tests pass (`uv run pytest tests/test_sync_checkout.py`). Ogun's own law applies to the town's tooling, not just its gap-reports: a false "diverged" is exactly the false-positive shape that erodes trust in an automated check, and this one would have silently blocked every future hour's recovery the same way.
